title: The monkey king and the bridge.
lines: This is a very old story from India.
It's about a wise monkey king.
On the bank of the great river Ganges stood an enormous mango tree.
Eighty thousand monkeys lived in that tree.
They were led by a big, strong monkey king.
The mangoes from that tree were the sweetest in the world.
Yellow and juicy.
Mmm!
The monkey king said to the monkeys: Be very careful.
Never let a mango fall into the river.
If people find our mangoes, they'll come to get them.
But one day a mango did fall into the water.
It floated away.
Far away.
To the city of the human king.
The human king was sitting by the river.
He saw the mango floating by.
He tasted it.
It was so sweet!
So delicious!
I want more of those mangoes!
The king went searching with his soldiers.
They followed the river.
For days.
Until they came to the big mango tree.
They saw the monkeys in the tree.
The king got angry.
Those monkeys are eating my mangoes!
Chase them away!
The soldiers came with bows and arrows.
The monkeys were very scared.
They jumped back and forth.
They didn't know where to go.
The monkey king thought fast.
On the other side of the river was a safe forest.
But the river was too wide.
The monkeys couldn't jump across.
The monkey king was very strong.
He took a long bamboo cane.
He tied it to his foot.
He jumped across the river.
He tied the cane to a tree on the other side.
But the bamboo cane was too short.
It didn't quite reach.
So the monkey king held on to a branch of the mango tree with his hands.
His own body became the last piece of the bridge.
Walk across me, he said to the monkeys.
Quickly!
One by one the monkeys walked across the bamboo.
And across their king's back.
Thousands and thousands of monkeys.
To the safe forest.
The monkey king's back hurt.
But he held on.
Until the very last monkey was across.
The human king saw it all.
He was quiet.
He had never seen anyone take such good care of his people.
He had the monkey king gently brought down.
He laid him on a soft blanket.
Why did you do that?
asked the king.
You could have escaped yourself.
The monkey king said: A true king takes care of his people first.
Only then of himself.
The human king bowed his head.
I will never forget that.
From then on he left the monkeys in peace.
And he became a better king himself.
The end.
